title: US Government Closes the Loophole: Remote AI Compute Now Under Strict Export Controls!
summary: The U.S. Department of Commerce has issued an interim final rule expanding export controls to remote cloud computing access of advanced AI power. The rule targets data centers exceeding 12 million Total Processing Performance to prevent restricted jurisdictions from bypassing hardware bans.
raw_text: So check this out, because the U.S. government just closed one of the biggest loopholes in tech history. For months, companies could bypass physical chip export bans to China by simply renting out massive cloud computing power overseas. Well, not anymore! The Department of Commerce just dropped a heavy interim final rule that officially classifies remote cloud AI compute as a controlled asset. If a data center hits over 12 million Total Processing Performance—which is roughly equal to 750 high-end Nvidia H100 or H200 GPUs—they need a specific license to serve restricted regions like China, Russia, and Iran. Honestly, this is huge for the semiconductor market. When this dropped, Nvidia shares took an immediate 3.9% hit, and companies like Intel and Micron saw drops over 6%. Cloud giants now have just 90 days to overhaul their Know Your Customer protocols or risk getting shut down. It's a total game-changer for global infrastructure, and it proves that governments are treating raw compute power just like physical military hardware. What do you think about these new cloud rules? title: New 'Verify by Doing' AI Framework Shatters Hallucination Loops Without Human Help!
summary: A newly published academic framework called the 'Verify by Doing' (VbD) architecture enables language models to self-improve and correct execution errors by co-evolving separate Actor and Evaluator software harnesses. The independent Evaluator programmatically interrogates artifacts, effectively eliminating AI hallucination loops.
raw_text: Here's a massive technical breakthrough that could finally solve the AI hallucination problem. A newly published academic framework called 'Verify by Doing'—or VbD—is changing how language models self-improve without needing human feedback. Instead of letting an AI judge its own work, the VbD architecture splits the system into two co-evolving software harnesses: an Actor that builds the solution, and an independent Evaluator that acts like a strict Quality Assurance engineer. The Evaluator runs active inspection tools, sandboxed code, and test scripts to programmatically interrogate everything the Actor produces. If something breaks, it hands back hard verifiable evidence, forcing the Actor to rewrite its code until all tests pass. Across benchmarks in finance, data science, and marketing workflows, this setup delivered clean performance boosts across the board. Honestly, treating AI development like professional software engineering with strict separation of duties is genius. This brings us one step closer to truly autonomous digital workers.
